candidates.name: Zagreb Cathedral
candidates.hours: It is closed due to March 2020 earthquake damage
candidates.content: The Zagreb Cathedral with its twin spires is the most well known landmark of the city. The original cathedral dates back to 1217 but the present structure dates to 1906. The chief architect was Hermann Bollé.

candidates.name: Typhlological Museum
candidates.price: Adults €3; students & schoolchildren €2; disabled & pensioners free
candidates.content: Rather specialised museum focusing on the history of institutions for the blind, writing systems for the blind and other visual impairments together with more modern developments. There is a dark room where you can experience what

candidates.name: Technical Museum Nikola Tesla
candidates.price: Adult €4, under 7 free, senior and student €3
candidates.content: Has a lot of technical inventions, fire engines, a cabinet of Nikola Tesla, a planetarium and an underground mine.

candidates.name: Museum of Illusions
candidates.content: Prepare to be deceived. A few exhibits are more suited to two people.

candidates.name: Mirogoj Cemetery
candidates.content: Mirogoj is the central cemetery of Zagreb. It was opened in 1876 north of the city centre. The mortuary, the impressive and picturesque arcades with the church of Christ the King (architect H. Bollé, 1883-1914) make it one of the

candidates.name: Museum of Contemporary Art
candidates.price: From about €4, scroll down visitor information page on website to see all prices; first Wednesday free
candidates.content: Follows and presents contemporary trends in fine arts.

candidates.name: Museum of Hangovers
candidates.content: Specialty museum about nightlife culture and hangovers; interactive exhibits and short visit (45–60 min).

candidates.name: Sabor Palace
candidates.content: The seat of the Croatian Parliament.

candidates.name: Croatian Museum of Naïve Art
candidates.content: Houses more than one thousand works belonging to Croatian naïve art.

candidates.name: Museum of Broken Relationships
candidates.content: What remains after a break-up? Museum's permanent display is an opportunity to experience a unique emotional journey through dozens of love leftovers collected from all around the world. Museum is also the winner of Kenneth Hudson

candidates.name: Klovićevi Dvori Gallery
candidates.content: This gallery in the old Jesuit monastery with changing exhibitions introduces Croatian and foreign cultural and artistic heritage across all eras. In most exhibitions, photography without flash is permitted.

candidates.name: Lotrščak Tower
candidates.content: Great local views if you are prepared to climb the spiral staircase.

candidates.name: Grič Tunnel
candidates.content: A 450-m-long pedestrian tunnel that was built as bomb shelter is sometimes used for concerts.

candidates.name: The Grounded Sun
candidates.content: Prizemljeno sunce by Ivan Kožarić is a 1971 sculpture, a 2-m-wide bronze sphere, which represents the scale model of the Sun, with 9 planets of the solar system in their scaled size compared to this Sun. Mercury is in Margaretska

candidates.name: Medvedgrad Castle and Medvednica
candidates.price: Visitor Centre Adults €7.95 (weekends), €6.6 (weekday) many other ticket options
candidates.content: The imposing mountain overlooking Zagreb (Medvednica) contains a preserved fortress (Medvedgrad) and fascinating views of the city. Being respectful in the fort is a good idea, since it is the site of the Altar of the Homeland mem

candidates.name: Jarun
candidates.content: Jarun Lake is a recreational area based around a large lake where locals go to relax, exercise - and party! The centrepiece of the area is the lake, which is used for windsurfing and has a large rowing section with spectator stand

candidates.name: St. Mark's Square
candidates.content: St. Mark's Church is known for its colourful roof tiles depicting the coat of arms of Croatia and Zagreb. St. Mark's Church was constructed in 1499.

candidates.name: Old Town Gate
candidates.content: now a shrine to virgin Mary - the "Kamenita vrata" where you can light a candle and, as the locals believe, your wish will be granted. Please be silent, even if just passing through the Gate. The portrait of Mary is said to be sac

candidates.name: Zagreb City Museum
candidates.content: The permanent collection tells the history of the city but there are also temporary exhibitions

candidates.name: Mažuranić Square
candidates.content: Named after Croatian poet Ivan Mažuranić.

candidates.name: Marulić Square
candidates.content: Marulić Square houses the Croatia State Archive, and a statue of Marko Marulić.

candidates.name: Republic of Croatia Square
candidates.content: One of the largest and greenest squares of Zagreb, with the Croatian National Theatre in its centre.

candidates.name: Mimara Museum
candidates.hours: Closed to public since the March 2020 earthquake
candidates.content: Houses some 3,700 works of art donated by Ante Topić Mimara. The collection comprises more than 1,500 exhibits dating from the prehistoric period up to the 20th century. Some of the most famous exhibits include works by Lorenzetti

candidates.name: Archaeological Museum
candidates.hours: Opening hours have been limited since the 2020 earthquake; check the website
candidates.content: Possesses over 400,000 objects, not all of them being exhibited. The holdings include evidence of Croatian presence in this area as well as rare samples which have made the museum known to the whole world. The most famous are the

candidates.name: Josip Račić Gallery
candidates.content: Second smaller site of the National Museum of Modern art hosting temporary exhibitions.

candidates.name: Bundek
candidates.content: Park with lake, hosts horticultural shows, firework festivals, workshops, concerts and music festivals (mostly during the summer).

candidates.name: St. Catherine's Church
candidates.content: Baroque style church

candidates.name: Modern Gallery
candidates.content: Exhibits fine artists of the 19th and 20th centuries.

candidates.name: Strossmayerovo šetalište
candidates.content: In the summer, it is an outdoor scene for painters, musicians and other artists offering food, drinks, performances and concerts. Popular meeting place for all ages, with a great view of the Lower Town.

candidates.name: Snow Queen Trophy
candidates.content: Ladies Night Slalom : Zagreb is the only capital in the world that hosts a Ski World Cup race. The slalom event - known as the "Snow Queen Trophy" (Snježna kraljica) - usually takes place in January. It is the most expensive race

candidates.name: Kino Tuškanac
candidates.price: Entrance for programs Kinoteka and Restauracije is free, regular ticket is €4
candidates.content: Showing much more than just European filmography, alternative and older films. Films are screened in their original language with only Croatian subtites.

candidates.name: Cineplexx Centar Kaptol
candidates.content: A multiplex cinema (5 screens) within the Kaptol Shopping Centre north of the Cathedral.

candidates.name: Cineplexx City Centre One East
candidates.content: A multiplex cinema (7 screens) on the east side of Zagreb.

candidates.name: Močvara
candidates.content: A local alternative club (rock, punk, metal, indie) with various concerts and theme nights/programmes. Sometimes hosts festivals, young indie talent concerts, movie nights, exhibitions.

candidates.name: KSET
candidates.price: Entrance prices from €1.5 (students) to €6-8 for concerts
candidates.content: A popular student club. Offers various indie and alternative programmes every night of the week. Indoors smoking prohibited. Serves only beer and non alcoholic drinks.

candidates.name: Cica
candidates.content: Bar mostly known for its great and varied choice of the local schnappses (rakija). Interesting always changing, gallery-like interior. The whole bar is small but offers outdoor seating. Very popular and crowded, brimming with youn

candidates.name: Funk club
candidates.content: Cafe and bar that offers various music night programmes in the basement (mostly alternative, DJs, world music) and spacial backpacker evenings. Very good atmosphere, lots of character, cheap and tasty Rakija shoots and excellent e

candidates.name: Melin
candidates.content: A cheap bar brimming with young people and students. Offers indoors, a roofed terraced leveled seating and an open terrace facing Tkalčićeva street. Known for crowds of people often drinking even around the bar, in the park and pl

candidates.name: Purgeraj
candidates.content: A bar/club in the Ribnjak park in the city centre. Offers mostly rock, blues and alternative music. Daily happy hour when you get two drinks for the price of one. Sometimes hosts concerts. Popular with student crowd esp on Thursda

candidates.name: Jabuka
candidates.content: Cult club for alternative, punk music. Cheap drinks opened on weekends, often concerts of alternative bands. Mostly visited on weekends, especially Fridays. Admission fee: €3.5.

candidates.name: Medika
candidates.content: A local alternative club/legalized squat usually loaded with people during weekends, playing various music genres until the early morning. Best Croatian beers for €1.5.

candidates.name: Booksa
candidates.content: A cafe, bookshop and library famous with local young intellectuals.

candidates.name: Golf
candidates.content: Popular golf-themed cafe/bar.

candidates.name: KIC
candidates.content: Offers free internet and cheap international call centre. Hosts a cinema with various alternative movies.

candidates.name: Kino Grič
candidates.content: Old cinema. Hosts movies, festivals, music nights and Zagreb's hipster crowd.

candidates.name: Mali Medo
candidates.content: Offers a good choice of local beer and food. Indoors smoking prohibited. Has a terrace facing Tkalčićeva street.

candidates.name: Mali Medo
candidates.content: Another traditional Croatian restaurant. Lively atmosphere, youthful clientele, and all very affordable. Excellent ćevapčići and gulaš, not to mention superb beer.

candidates.name: Taquitos Bandidos
candidates.content: Exactly what street food should be. Simple, fast, tasty and well thought out creative dishes that surprise you and overdeliver. Try their amazing chipotle sauce! It's Mexican street food.

candidates.name: Nocturno
candidates.content: Good place to try the local gastronomy. An excellent restaurant with a variety of offers and helpful staff and a pleasant atmosphere.

candidates.name: MS Grill Restaurant
candidates.content: It's a family owned local restaurant. The staff is very nice and welcoming

candidates.name: Zrno bio bistro
candidates.content: Almost all vegan and organic. Some ingredients come from their own Zrno farm, less than an hour away. Mains rich in umami, luscious desserts. An extensive beer and wine list.

candidates.name: Takenoko
candidates.content: Zagreb may not be synonymous with sushi restaurants, but this one is superb. It is not cheap, but the sushi they make is incredible.

candidates.name: Vincek
candidates.content: The local, best-known ice cream and cake palace in town centre. Offers diet foods.

candidates.name: Sandwich Bar Pingvin
candidates.content: Classic sandwich bar with a wide menu and reasonably good mix of languages. One of the most popular dishes is the toplo/hladno (hot/cold), a grilled chicken and vegetables sandwich.

candidates.name: Koykan Gajeva
candidates.content: Italian piadinas, Japanese teriyaki sticks, oriental wraps, Bubble tea from Taiwan and Japanese mochi cakes.

candidates.name: The Cookie Factory
candidates.content: Homebaked American sweets. Cookies, brownies and bars, krispy treats, muffins, cupcakes, banana breads, scones, cobblers, biscotti, top notch coffee, smoothies, cakes and pies.

candidates.name: La Štruk
candidates.content: One of Zagreb's oldest fast food spots. Highly recommended are the grilled cheese sandwich, the grilled stuffed lungic and the zagrebacki sandwich.

candidates.name: Plac Kitchen & Grill
candidates.content: Tasty Cevapcici sausages, fast service and not expensive. Fantastic peppers, cevapi and great special burgers. The restaurant is a bit hidden.

december.text: Zagreb is a vibrant city of around 770,000 people (2021, metropolitan area: 1,100,000). In 2017 it was visited by over a million tourists, mainly from Austria, Germany and Italy.
